chapter_title: Concerning the Four Archetypes that occur in the E

fills.notes: The sentence defines four hidden aspects in humans that enable perception; in the oldest cosmological register these are the elemental degrees (fire, water, wind/air, earth) present as an interior structure of the body and senses.

fills.fill: and the four powers that are hidden in them
fills.notes: The text distinguishes (a) perceivable aspects and (b) the hidden enabling forces within; the parallelism calls for a second tetrad: powers/forces within the elements/senses rather than external doctrines.

The phrase “they belong …” requires an antecedent to which the four aspects correspond; “roots” matches Iranian/elemental cosmology and the correspondential idiom (roots as first natural receptacles).

fills.fill: from them the body is woven
fills.notes: Concludes the correspondential claim: without the hidden tetrad, the human form cannot function; “woven” fits the substrate’s impersonal craft-language for composition from elements.
The clause “... that is in the ... belongs to the fire” needs a quality assigned to fire; heat is the proper correspondential property (fire as active ardor/energy in ultimates).
In this substrate, blood corresponds to the fiery element as life-heat in the body; it also contrasts well with “darkness belongs to the abyss” and “living air” as the clarifying perceiver.
Direct continuation of the day/night contrast: the pupil cannot perceive at night. The point then turns to the ‘mystery’ (correspondence) of that limitation.
The mystery being expounded is precisely the alternation of day/night as states of light and obscuration; naming “night” keeps the register concrete before it is unfolded cosmologically.
The ‘door’ below aligns with the abyss in ¶2 (darkness belongs to the abyss). The eye’s incapacity at night corresponds to the lower gate by which obscuration rises.
The syntax needs a verbal link: the ‘door … below’ is positioned with respect to the cardinal points; “set/placed” is the expected structural verb in the impersonal cosmological voice.
In correspondential cosmology, the ‘door below’ associated with night and descent aligns with the West (setting, obscuration), contrasted with the upper region of light.
Balances the previous: the ‘mystery … is the door’ in the lower/western quarter, while the opposite quarter is ‘above’ (rising/light) in the east.
“He has … great …” calls for an attribute of the upper region/source that sends down living powers; “glory” fits the oldest layer’s impersonal radiance-language without importing devotional titles.
What “came down … living …” are not persons but dynamic agencies; “living powers” is the natural phrase in the substrate for the descending forces by which First Man ‘knew all things’.

assessment: Most gaps are restorable by the chapter’s correspondential structure: a tetradic anthropology (elements/powers), elemental attributions (fire/heat/blood), and the day–night/above–below mapping onto East–West and the abyssal ‘door’. Exact original lexemes (e.g., whether the first tetrad is explicitly ‘elements’ or ‘members/senses’) remain somewhat open, but the required cosmological relations tightly constrain the fills.
